h1: Our Eco Farm — a streamside farmstay in a Makham garden so quiet you can hear the water flow
intro: If you're looking for a Chanthaburi stay that takes you out of the city, away from the beach, and into real nature — waking up to the sound of a stream, green trees all around, and cool fresh air — Our Eco Farm (Baan Eco Farm) is a name that people who love quiet, nature-close stays in Makham District keep mentioning · it's a tiny farmstay in a streamside working garden in Tambon Pathawi that guests remember for its quiet, cleanliness, friendly staff, and a closeness to nature that's hard to find in ordinary places to stay · with only around 13 rooms, from about THB 1,000/night, and pets welcome · real-review scores are high at around 9.5 from 11 reviews on Trip.com and 8.2 from 267 reviews on Agoda

body.html: The big picture and who it suits — to put it the way a friend would, Our Eco Farm, or what many people call "Baan Eco Farm," is a very small farmstay tucked away in a streamside working garden at Ban Pong Rong Sen, Tambon Pathawi, Makham District, Chanthaburi · what clearly sets it apart from the usual Chanthaburi stays is that it isn't selling the sea, isn't selling the city, and isn't selling an infinity pool or luxe design — it's selling "farm and nature," exactly as the name says · it's a stay in the middle of a garden, lots of trees, a stream running through, the cool comfortable air of Chanthaburi's semi-mountainous areas, and so quiet that many guests say all they hear is the water and the birds · with only around 13 rooms, the place feels private, more like staying at a friend's farmhouse than checking into a hotel · from real reviews across several platforms, the people who come away most impressed tend to be couples or anyone who wants to escape the chaos and be somewhere quiet with nature and animal lovers who want to bring their dog or cat along, because this is a pet-friendly stay · another group it fits well is people who work and want a quiet corner to rest their mind, read a book, or do a workation in a setting where things genuinely slow down · on the flip side, if you're after a beachfront stay with full big-resort facilities, restaurants and convenience stores within walking distance, or rooms with polished design in every corner, this may not be your answer, because its identity is a "quiet, nature-close farmstay that's good value," not a fully-loaded luxury resort · the farm has been open since around 2015, is still running today, and still earns high review scores, especially for service and atmosphere, which keeps it on the radar of anyone who loves nature-style stays in the east

Location and getting there — Makham District is a semi-mountainous area in the eastern part of Chanthaburi province, a zone known for fruit orchards — durian, rambutan, mangosteen — and lush green nature, which is different from the seaside Chanthaburi most people are familiar with · Our Eco Farm itself sits at Ban Pong Rong Sen, Tambon Pathawi, set well back along a garden route, a fair distance from Chanthaburi town · from Bangkok it's about a 4-hour drive via the motorway and Sukhumvit Road heading toward Chanthaburi, then turning onto the Makham District route · the nearest sights around it are Wat Pong Rong Sen, just about 0.5 km away, and Wat Khao Manorom, about 2.3 km away · within a short drive there are also local villagers' farms and gardens to drop by, plus natural waterways to cool off in · for anyone wanting to continue on to Chanthaburi's well-known sights such as Phlio Waterfall or the park areas around Khao Soi Dao, you can drive on from here in not too long · an important point to be honest about is that this place is deep within the garden area, and the entrance at night is quite isolated and dark, as some reviews warn, so having your own car is practically essential, since public transport around here is very scarce, and driving back to the stay in the evening calls for care and extra time · the farm has a shuttle service, which helps for those who don't drive themselves, but you should ask and arrange it in advance · if you fly in, landing at U-Tapao Airport (UTP) and then continuing by rental car is the most convenient option

"Staying here felt like a reset. So quiet you can hear the water flowing and the birds, green trees all around, cool comfortable air · the staff are so lovely, they look after you like family, and there's an adorable farm dog too. The breakfast is fresh-cooked and delicious — it's a place I want to come back to and sleep quietly again."

Room types and the look — Our Eco Farm has only around 13 rooms, which is very small and part of the charm here, because it keeps the atmosphere quiet and private · the rooms break down mainly into Superior rooms with a queen bed and Standard rooms with a queen bed, differing slightly in size and small details, and suited mainly to two people · the decor is simple and easy on the eye, blending with the garden and the nature around it rather than going for flashy luxury, with a warm farmhouse tone · every room is air-conditioned, with a flat-screen satellite TV, a fridge, free bottled drinking water, free toiletries, a shower in the bathroom, and a private balcony to sit out on, catch the breeze, look at the garden, or listen to the stream · most real reviews agree in praising that the rooms are very clean — a high-scoring point (cleanliness around 9.4 on Trip.com), the beds are comfortable, and the surroundings are so shady and green you feel relaxed the moment you open the door · many people love waking up to a view of the green garden and the cool morning air · worth knowing: because it's a small nature-focused farmstay, the rooms emphasize cleanliness and comfort over luxury, so if you expect five-star hotel specs with everything high-tech, understand this identity before you book · a few reviews mention small details like a door that sticks a bit, which is a minor thing you'll find at farmhouse-style stays

Facilities and activities — even though it's a small farmstay, Our Eco Farm provides the essentials for a nature-close getaway in its own way · the heart of it is the streamside location in a working garden, which gives a cool, quiet atmosphere, with a garden, a terrace, and a sun deck (solarium) to lounge in · there's BBQ service for those who want to grill their own food in the garden setting, and fishing for anyone who wants to sit and chill by the water · many reviews mention getting to play in the stream or the creek near the stay, an activity kids and adults both enjoy on a hot day · the resort has a shuttle service, laundry/dry cleaning, luggage storage, postal service, VIP check-in for some rooms, free private parking, and free Wi-Fi in the common areas · what sets it apart from ordinary stays is that it's a pet-friendly stay, dogs and cats both welcome, something animal lovers seek out · to be honest, there's no swimming pool, gym, or spa like a big resort — the selling point is nature, the stream, and the quiet, so if you're planning to come for a pool soak or full facilities, this may not fit, but if you come to "be with nature," this farm gives you what big resorts can't

Food and dining — Our Eco Farm has a restaurant and coffee shop on site, plus room service · the point that consistently earns praise in real reviews is the breakfast, which many say is freshly made and delicious — reviews mention dishes like sausages, scrambled eggs, and rice porridge, served in a quiet garden setting that makes the morning meal an especially relaxing time · breakfast is served around 7:00–9:00 AM (some room packages may charge extra for breakfast, so check when booking) · lunch and dinner can be ordered at the restaurant, or you can use the BBQ service to grill in the garden, an activity that suits the farm atmosphere · an honest note: because this place is deep within the garden area, there are no restaurants or convenience stores within easy walking distance, so if you want to eat out you'll need to drive a fair way — many people therefore choose to let the farm's kitchen handle their meals, or bring their own food in the car · overall the food here is at a "good and genuine" farmhouse level, especially the breakfast, which guests mention positively most often · for those who love nature, eating fresh-cooked food in a garden setting is part of the charm of staying here

Service — service is the most-praised aspect here and the main reason the overall score is high, with the service score on Trip.com reaching around 9.8 · many real reviews agree that the staff and the farm owners are warm and friendly, looking after you with the same care you'd give a relative visiting home, helping recommend places to visit, helping with travel, and looking after you from check-in to check-out · an interesting point is that the team speaks several languages — Thai, English, German, and Dutch, which makes international guests feel comfortable and communication easy, reflecting that this place welcomes travelers from many countries well · the friendly farm atmosphere, along with the farm dogs and cats that many reviews mention fondly, makes many guests feel especially at home · for a stay at this price point, service is clearly a very strong point · to be straightforward, since it's a small family-run farm, some services aren't staffed 24 hours a day like a big hotel, and certain requests may need to be arranged in advance, which is more the nature of this kind of stay than a downside

What real reviews say — the good and the not-so-good — pulling together Trip.com, Agoda, and other platforms, the picture lines up fairly well · on Trip.com the average is high at around 9.5 from 11 reviews, while Agoda sits at around 8.2 from 267 reviews, which when averaged together makes it a stay that guests are happy with at a good level · On the praise side: the quiet and the nature-close streamside atmosphere are mentioned most, along with the cleanliness of the rooms (around 9.4), the service and friendliness of the staff that scores especially high (around 9.8), the fresh-cooked delicious breakfast, getting to play in the stream, the adorable farm dogs and cats, and the value for the experience you get · couples and people wanting to escape the chaos rate the quiet and the service especially highly · On the watch-out side: the thing mentioned most is the deep location, with an entrance that's isolated and dark at night, making the evening drive back something to be careful about, the fact that there are no shops or restaurants within easy walking distance, the simple facilities with no swimming pool, and small details like a door that sticks a little · most of these gripes can be solved by setting the right expectation — that this is a nature-close farmstay built around quiet and privacy, not a resort in the middle of a tourist hub

"Clean room, very quiet, genuinely good for relaxing with nature. The owner and staff are lovely, speak several languages, and look after you above the price · the only knock is that the entrance at night is fairly dark and isolated, so you have to be a bit careful driving back, but once you reach the stay it's well worth it — quiet, comfortable, and a full night's sleep."

Price and value — to be honest, this isn't a luxury resort, and it never set out to be · the real selling point is getting to stay in a streamside farmstay in a garden — quiet, clean, with warm service — at a very approachable price · rooms start at around THB 1,000/night in normal periods (average around THB 1,300), which is very cheap for the nature-close experience you get · a Superior room with a queen bed nudges up a little depending on the season · compared with seaside Chanthaburi stays like the Chao Lao Beach area starting around THB 1,600 and up, or resorts in town, Our Eco Farm feels worthwhile in that you get quiet nature, privacy, and very highly rated service at a lower starting price · if you're planning a stay focused on genuinely resting, want to be with nature, are bringing a pet, or want a different kind of stay away from the beach and the city, every baht you spend here comes back in full in a way you won't find at an ordinary resort · but if you want the convenience of easily going out to eat and explore, full facilities, or to be near the sea, you'll have to weigh whether a location this deep suits your trip

Things to know before booking — there are several things that help make the stay smoother · one, understand first that this is a nature-close farmstay set deep within the garden area, not a resort in the middle of a tourist hub — set the right expectation and you'll be happy with the quiet you get · two, driving yourself is the most convenient, because the entrance is deep and public transport is scarce; there's free parking, and if you're not driving you should ask about the shuttle service in advance · three, the entrance is fairly dark and isolated at night, so plan to get back to the stay before evening, or drive carefully and allow extra time · four, since there are no convenience stores or restaurants to walk to nearby, bring the food and essentials you need in the car, or let the farm's kitchen handle your meals · five, if you're bringing a pet, give advance notice, because this is a pet-friendly stay and there are dogs and cats living on the farm too · six, with only around 13 rooms, during the cool-season high season and the fruit season (durian, rambutan, mangosteen, around April–June) rooms fill up fast, so book ahead and compare prices across several platforms

The bottom line — from all the real reviews, Our Eco Farm is the Chanthaburi stay for anyone seeking quiet, streamside nature, and warm service at an approachable price · a tiny farmstay of just 13 rooms in a working garden in Makham District, offering privacy, clean rooms, fresh-cooked breakfast, pets welcome, and staff who look after you like family and speak several languages, which makes it a place where people wanting to escape the chaos and be with nature can do so with peace of mind · if you're looking for a beachfront stay with full facilities and a swimming pool, or want to easily walk out to restaurants, this may not be your answer, and you should consider a resort on the Chao Lao Beach side or in Chanthaburi town instead · but for a slow nature trip where you want a comfortable, quiet, clean place to sleep, can bring your pet, and get the kind of attention from owners that big resorts can't provide — Baan Eco Farm does that job well and is good value, just as its high real-review scores for both service and cleanliness confirm

honestSummary: Our Eco Farm is the Chanthaburi stay for anyone seeking quiet, streamside nature, and warm service at an approachable price — a tiny farmstay of just 13 rooms in a Makham garden, with clean rooms, fresh-cooked breakfast, pets welcome, and multilingual staff · it's not a beachfront resort or fully equipped with facilities, and the location is deep so you need your own car, but for a slow nature trip it delivers neatly and is good value
honestChecks: If you don't have your own car — this place is deep within the garden area, public transport is scarce, and the entrance is isolated and dark at night → you should drive yourself, or ask about the farm's shuttle service in advance, and plan to get back before evening
If you want full big-resort facilities — this is a small family-run farmstay with no swimming pool or spa → set the right expectation and you'll be happy with the quiet and the nature you get

If you're planning mainly to visit the beach or Chanthaburi town — the farm is in semi-mountainous Makham District, a fair distance from the sea and the town → if the beach is the focus choose a stay in the Chao Lao Beach area, or if the city is the focus choose a stay in town instead

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Our Eco Farm Chanthaburi

faq.q: Where is Our Eco Farm and how do you get there?
faq.a: It's located at Ban Pong Rong Sen, Tambon Pathawi, Makham District, Chanthaburi, a semi-mountainous garden area, not the seaside side · from Bangkok it's about a 4-hour drive, with free parking · the entrance is deep and isolated and dark at night, so we recommend having your own car, or asking about the farm's shuttle service in advance, since public transport around here is very scarce

faq.q: What's the starting price at Our Eco Farm and what rooms are there?
faq.a: Rooms start at around THB 1,000/night in normal periods (average around THB 1,300) · there are Standard and Superior rooms with queen beds, suited to 2 guests · there are only around 13 rooms, and during the cool season and fruit season they fill up fast, so book ahead and compare across several platforms before booking

faq.q: Can you bring pets to stay?
faq.a: Yes · Our Eco Farm is a pet-friendly stay (dogs/cats), and the farm itself has dogs and cats that many reviews mention fondly · if you're bringing yours along, give the stay advance notice when booking for convenience

faq.q: What is there to do here and who is it for?
faq.a: It suits couples and anyone wanting to escape the chaos and be somewhere quiet with nature · the highlights are a stream to play in, a working garden to stroll, BBQ service and fishing, and a cool comfortable atmosphere good for relaxing and a workation · there's no swimming pool or big-resort facilities; the charm is in the quiet and the nature

faq.q: What are the review scores like and what are the gripes?
faq.a: Real-review scores are high at around 9.5 from 11 reviews on Trip.com and 8.2 from 267 reviews on Agoda · the most-praised points are service (around 9.8), the quiet nature-close setting, clean rooms, fresh-cooked breakfast, and warm owners who speak several languages · the gripes are about the deep location, the isolated, dark entrance at night, no shops nearby, and simple facilities with no swimming pool
